## Project Overview

Mocha is a general-purpose, flexible JavaScript testing framework for Node.js and the browser. [PROJECT_CHARTER.md:9-12][package.json] The package describes itself as a “classic, reliable, trusted test framework for Node.js and the browser.” [package.json]

The main implementation is JavaScript, with CommonJS, ESM, and browser-oriented modules visible under `lib/`, plus TypeScript declaration files. [lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][lib/nodejs/esm-utils.cjs:143-165][lib/types.d.ts:19-22] Rollup generates the browser bundle, and the documentation site uses Astro Starlight. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-65][docs/README.md:1-6]

Likely entry points include `bin/mocha.js` for the command-line executable, `lib/mocha.cjs` for the main Mocha API, and `browser-entry.js` for browser usage. [bin/mocha.js:41-46][lib/mocha.cjs:168-173][browser-entry.js:90-100] The CLI defaults to the `test` path when no test specification is supplied. [lib/cli/cli.js:80-82]

## Setup / Installation

Install Node.js `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`; Node.js 22 LTS is recommended. [AGENTS.md:22-27] npm is the required package manager; the repository explicitly says not to use Yarn or pnpm. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12]

Google Chrome is required for running browser tests locally. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12] The package engine requirement matches the documented Node.js prerequisite. [package.json]

From the repository root, install dependencies with:

```sh
npm install
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19][AGENTS.md:47-53]

For a clean CI-style installation, use `npm ci --ignore-scripts`; normal local bootstrap uses `npm install`. [AGENTS.md:47-53] Some optional dependencies may fail during `npm install`; the development guide says these failures can generally be ignored unless building documentation. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19]

Documentation work has a separate package installation step:

```sh
cd docs
npm install
```

[AGENTS.md:47-53] The documentation package uses Astro, Starlight, TypeScript, and related Astro integrations. [docs/package.json]

The supplied setup instructions do not identify any required application environment variables. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19] The repository ignores `.env` and `.env.test` files, but the evidence does not define values for them. [.gitignore]

## Running Locally

Run the full validation suite with:

```sh
npm test
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34] The repository also provides targeted commands such as `npm run test-smoke`, `npm run test-node:unit`, `npm run test-node:integration`, `npm run test-node:interfaces`, `npm run test-node:reporters`, `npm run test-browser`, `npm run tsc`, and `npm run lint`. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-45]

For a fast local edit-test loop, run:

```sh
npx mocha --watch test/unit/
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:46-50] Mocha’s watch mode reruns tests when watched files change, and the `rs` command followed by Enter schedules another run. [docs/src/content/docs/running/cli.mdx:522-529]

Build generated browser artifacts with:

```sh
npm run clean
npm run build
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-65] The build uses Rollup, while `clean` removes `mocha.js` and `mocha.js.map`. [package.json] Do not edit those generated bundle files directly. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-65]

Browser testing is normally run with:

```sh
npm run test-browser
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-45] The `test-browser` script cleans, builds, and then runs the browser test scripts, so it prepares the generated bundle before Playwright runs. [package.json][AGENTS.md:87-92]

The documentation site can be developed with:

```sh
cd docs
npm install
npm run generate
npm run dev
```

[docs/README.md:7-17] The evidence does not specify a port for the main project or the documentation development server. [docs/README.md:7-17][docs/package.json]

## Project Structure

- `bin/` contains the command-line executable; `bin/mocha.js` includes CLI option handling. [bin/mocha.js:41-46]
- `lib/` contains the core runtime and API implementation, including `lib/mocha.cjs`, suites, tests, runners, hooks, contexts, errors, plugins, reporters, and Node.js utilities. [lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][lib/suite.js:417-445][lib/runner.js:1202-1224][lib/plugin-loader.js:260-283]
- `lib/cli/` contains CLI parsing, configuration, file lookup, run helpers, watch handling, and option metadata. [lib/cli/cli.js:80-97][lib/cli/config.cjs:17-26][lib/cli/run-helpers.cjs:159-176][lib/cli/watch-run.cjs:444-500]
- `lib/reporters/` contains built-in reporters such as HTML, JSON, JSON stream, TAP, and XUnit implementations. [lib/reporters/html.js:58-88][lib/reporters/json.js:108-123][lib/reporters/json-stream.js:66-87][lib/reporters/tap.js:150-185][lib/reporters/xunit.js:119-148]
- `lib/nodejs/` contains Node-specific worker, ESM, serialization, and parallel-runner modules. [lib/nodejs/buffered-worker-pool.cjs:85-93][lib/nodejs/esm-utils.cjs:143-165][lib/nodejs/parallel-buffered-runner.cjs:289-298]
- `browser-entry.js` and `lib/browser/` contain browser entry and browser-specific behavior. [browser-entry.js:90-100][lib/browser/highlight-tags.js:32-37][lib/browser/parse-query.js:8-22]
- `test/unit/` contains unit tests for core modules such as context, errors, Mocha, runners, suites, and utilities. [test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-8][test/unit/mocha.spec.cjs:84-93][test/unit/runner.spec.cjs:28-30][test/unit/suite.spec.cjs:12-14]
- `test/node-unit/` contains Node-focused unit tests for CLI, worker, serialization, and parallel-runner modules. [test/node-unit/cli/cli.spec.js:12-14][test/node-unit/worker.spec.cjs:191-193][test/node-unit/serializer.spec.cjs:12-14]
- `test/integration/` contains integration tests, option tests, plugin tests, regression tests, and fixtures. [test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/integration/options/watch.spec.cjs:38-40][test/integration/plugins/global-fixtures.spec.cjs:148-152][test/integration/fixtures/passing.fixture.cjs:6-12]
- `test/reporters/` contains reporter tests, while `test/browser-specific/` contains browser-specific tests and fixtures. [test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52][test/reporters/json.spec.js:23-25][test/browser-specific/esm.spec.js:7-9]
- `docs/` is a separate Astro Starlight documentation package with content under `docs/src/content/docs/`. [docs/README.md:1-6][docs/package.json][docs/tsconfig.json]
- `example/config/` contains configuration examples intended to illustrate available options rather than serve as boilerplates. [example/config/README.md:1-7]
- `repro/` is an optional, separate minimal Node project for reproducing end-user behavior against the checkout. [repro/README.md:1-9][repro/README.md:12-35]

## Testing

The repository uses Mocha’s own test runner for Node and browser-oriented test suites, with Playwright used for browser tests. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-45][package.json] Supporting test dependencies include `@playwright/test`, Chai, Sinon, Unexpected, NYC, and related tooling. [package.json]

Run all code validations with:

```sh
npm test
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34] The visible validation commands include smoke tests, Node unit and integration suites, interface and reporter tests, browser tests, TypeScript checking, linting, and formatting checks. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-45]

The main test locations include `test/unit/`, `test/node-unit/`, `test/integration/`, `test/interfaces/`, `test/reporters/`, `test/only/`, `test/require/`, `test/smoke/`, and `test/browser-specific/`. [test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-8][test/node-unit/mocha.spec.cjs:91-93][test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/interfaces/bdd.spec.js:25-27][test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52][test/only/bdd-require.spec.cjs:10-12][test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14][test/browser-specific/esm.spec.js:7-9]

The repository’s test files use Mocha suites and test cases, including `describe`, `it`, and interface-specific `test` calls. [test/integration/fixtures/passing-sync.fixture.js:3-6][test/interfaces/qunit.spec.js:3-5] Tests commonly use `beforeEach` and `afterEach` hooks, with Sinon cleanup visible in unit and reporter tests. [test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-13][test/unit/errors.spec.cjs:9-11][test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52]

For focused development, run the smoke suite with:

```sh
npm run test-smoke
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-45] A unit-test watch cycle can be run with:

```sh
npx mocha --watch test/unit/
```

[.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:46-50]

Browser tests require the generated browser bundle; the repository recommends running `npm run test-browser`, which performs the clean-and-build sequence before Playwright tests. [AGENTS.md:87-92][package.json] The supplied evidence does not identify a single shared test setup file; setup behavior appears in individual test files and fixtures. [test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-13][test/integration/fixtures/plugins/root-hooks/root-hook-defs-a.fixture.js:4-15]
